normalization.relation: memory_blob(memory_id, session_id, turn_no, agent_model, session_day, body, entities[], fact_text, fact_id, source, confidence)
normalization.violation: entities[] is a repeating group held inside one attribute.
normalization.rule: A relation is in 1NF when every attribute holds a single atomic value.
normalization.anomaly: You cannot ask "which memories mention SVC-4470" without parsing an array in application code, so the DBMS cannot index it.
normalization.fix: Project the repeating group into MEMORY_ENTITY, keyed by (memory_id, entity_id).

normalization.relation: memory_flat(memory_id, session_id, turn_no, agent_model, session_day, body, fact_text, fact_id, source, confidence)
normalization.violation: session_day depends on session_id alone, which is only part of the natural key (session_id, turn_no).
normalization.rule: A relation is in 2NF when no non-prime attribute is partially dependent on a candidate key.
normalization.anomaly: A session's date is restated on every memory it produced. Correcting it means rewriting every row, and missing one splits the session in two.

normalization.relation: memory_2nf(memory_id, session_id, turn_no, agent_model, body, fact_text, fact_id, source, confidence)
normalization.violation: memory_id → session_id → agent_model is a transitive dependency.
normalization.rule: A relation is in 3NF when no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on a candidate key.
normalization.anomaly: The agent model is stored once per memory rather than once per session. It cannot be corrected atomically, and a session with no memories cannot record which model ran it at all.
normalization.fix: Move agent_model into AGENT and reference it from SESSION.

normalization.relation: memory_3nf(memory_id, session_id, turn_no, body, fact_text, fact_id, source, confidence)
normalization.violation: fact_id → fact_text, and fact_id is not a superkey of MEMORY.
normalization.rule: A relation is in BCNF when every determinant is a candidate key.
normalization.anomaly: This is the one that hurts an agent. The same fact is restated across many memories; when the fact changes, every restatement is now a claim the agent will retrieve and believe. §6.7 measures how many contradictions this produces.
normalization.fix: Move fact_text into FACT and leave MEMORY holding only the reference.

normalization.relation: memory(memory_id, session_id, turn_no, seq, kind, body, fact_id, created_day, source, confidence, superseded_by)
normalization.rule: Every determinant is a candidate key.
normalization.fix: This is the schema the SQLite and Postgres arms were measured on.
